metadata.title: Earning Income, Commission, and Australian Taxation
metadata.vcaa_description: Use mathematical modelling to solve practical problems involving direct proportion, rates, ratios and percentages, including in financial contexts.
metadata.target_mastery: Calculate gross pay including time-and-a-half/double-time overtime, tiered commission, leave loading (17.5%), and Australian PAYG progressive income tax.

key_vocabulary.definition: Higher hourly pay rates paid for hours worked beyond standard full-time hours, commonly time-and-a-half ($1.5 \times \text{normal rate}$) or double time ($2.0 \times \text{normal rate}$).
Income earned as a percentage of the value of goods sold, often combined with a fixed base payment called a retainer.
An extra allowance of $17.5\%$ added to $4$ weeks of normal pay during annual holiday leave in many Australian awards.

Taxable income equals gross income minus allowable tax deductions. Under Australia's progressive PAYG tax system, higher marginal rates apply only to the portion of taxable income above each bracket threshold.

theory.title: Wages, Salaries, Overtime, and Holiday Leave Loading
theory.explanation: A wage earner is paid an hourly rate $r$ for each hour worked, whereas a salary earner receives a fixed annual amount divided across $52$ weeks or $26$ fortnights (for accounting accuracy, $1\text{ year} = 52\text{ weeks} = 26\text{ fortnights} = 12\text{ months}$). Overtime hours worked beyond standard hours are paid at time-and-a-half ($1.5r$) or double time ($2r$). Under many Australian employment awards, $4$-week annual holiday pay includes a $17.5\%$ leave loading bonus.
theory.formula_latex: \text{Gross Wage} = h_{\text{norm}} r + h_{1.5}(1.5r) + h_{2.0}(2r), \quad \text{Holiday Pay (4 wks)} = 4w \times 1.175
theory.callout_title: Convert Between Annual Salary and Weekly Pay Carefully
theory.callout_rule: To convert an annual salary to weekly pay, divide by $52$ (or by $26$ for fortnightly pay). Multiply by $1.175$ to include the $17.5\%$ holiday leave loading on $4$ weeks of pay.

theory.title: Retainers and Tiered Sales Commission
theory.explanation: Salespeople such as real-estate agents and car dealers often earn a fixed retainer plus a percentage commission on sales. In a tiered (sliding-scale) commission scheme, one percentage rate applies to sales up to a specified threshold, and a different percentage rate applies only to the sales amount exceeding that threshold.
theory.formula_latex: \text{Total Earnings} = \text{Retainer} + r_1 T + r_2 (\text{Sales} - T) \quad (\text{for } \text{Sales} > T)
theory.callout_title: Tiered Rates Apply Only to the Excess Above the Threshold

theory.title: Australian Progressive Income Tax and the Medicare Levy
theory.explanation: Taxable income is calculated by subtracting work-related tax deductions from gross annual income. Under the 2024–25 Australian Resident Income Tax rates: $\$0\text{–}\$18\,200$ is tax-free; $\$18\,201\text{–}\$45\,000$ is taxed at $16\text{c}$ per $\$1$ over $\$18\,200$; $\$45\,001\text{–}\$135\,000$ is $\$4288$ plus $30\text{c}$ per $\$1$ over $\$45\,000$; $\$135\,001\text{–}\$190\,000$ is $\$31\,288$ plus $37\text{c}$ per $\$1$ over $\$135\,000$; and over $\$190\,000$ is $\$51\,638$ plus $45\text{c}$ per $\$1$ over $\$190\,000$. Most taxpayers also pay a $2\%$ Medicare levy on their entire taxable income.
theory.callout_title: Crossing Into a Higher Tax Bracket Never Reduces Net Pay
theory.callout_rule: Only the dollars earned ABOVE a bracket threshold are taxed at the higher marginal rate — all income below the threshold stays taxed at the lower rates.

worked_examples.title: Calculating Weekly Gross Pay with Overtime
worked_examples.problem: Chloe works as an apprentice electrician in Ballarat at a normal rate of $\$28\text{/h}$. In one week she works $38$ normal hours, $4$ hours at time-and-a-half, and $3$ hours on Sunday at double time. Calculate her gross weekly pay.

steps.thinking: Calculate her normal pay for $38$ hours at $\$28\text{/h}$, time-and-a-half pay for $4$ hours at $1.5 \times \$28 = \$42\text{/h}$, and double-time pay for $3$ hours at $2 \times \$28 = \$56\text{/h}$.
Sum the three components to find Chloe's total gross pay for the week.

now_you_try.problem: Liam earns $\$24\text{/h}$ for a standard $35$-hour week, plus $6$ hours at time-and-a-half and $2$ hours at double time. Find his gross weekly pay.
now_you_try.hint: Time-and-a-half is $\$36\text{/h}$ and double time is $\$48\text{/h}$.

worked_examples.title: Tiered Commission with a Weekly Retainer
worked_examples.problem: A software sales representative in Melbourne receives a weekly retainer of $\$650$, plus $4\%$ commission on the first $\$20\,000$ of weekly sales and $6.5\%$ on all sales exceeding $\$20\,000$. Calculate her total earnings in a week where her sales total $\$34\,000$.

steps.thinking: Add the weekly retainer of $\$650$ to the total commission.

now_you_try.problem: A real-estate agent earns $2.5\%$ commission on the first $\$600\,000$ of a property's sale price and $1.5\%$ on the remainder above $\$600\,000$. Find the total commission on a house sold for $\$840\,000$.

worked_examples.title: Calculating Australian Income Tax and Medicare Levy
worked_examples.problem: An engineer in Adelaide has a gross annual salary of $\$98\,400$ and allowable work-related deductions of $\$3400$. Using the 2024–25 resident tax bracket ($\$45\,001\text{–}\$135\,000$: $\$4288$ plus $30\text{c}$ for each $\$1$ over $\$45\,000$), calculate: (a) her taxable income, (b) her income tax payable, and (c) her $2\%$ Medicare levy.

steps.thinking: Subtract allowable deductions from gross income to find taxable income.

Since $\$95\,000$ lies in the $\$45\,001\text{–}\$135\,000$ bracket, add $\$4288$ to $30\%$ of the excess above $\$45\,000$ ($\$95\,000 - \$45\,000 = \$50\,000$), and compute $2\%$ of $\$95\,000$ for the Medicare levy.

now_you_try.problem: A teacher has a gross income of $\$84\,200$ and tax deductions of $\$2200$. Using the same bracket ($\$4288 + 30\%$ of excess over $\$45\,000$), find their taxable income and income tax payable.
now_you_try.hint: Taxable income is $\$82\,000$, which is $\$37\,000$ over $\$45\,000$.

common_misconceptions.title: Applying the Top Marginal Tax Rate to the Entire Taxable Income
common_misconceptions.misconception: Thinking that a worker with a taxable income of $\$50\,000$ in the $30\%$ bracket pays $0.30 \times \$50\,000 = \$15\,000$ in income tax.
common_misconceptions.correct_concept: In a progressive tax system, the first $\$18\,200$ is taxed at $0\%$, the slice from $\$18\,200$ to $\$45\,000$ is taxed at $16\%$ ($\$4288$), and only the $\$5000$ above $\$45\,000$ is taxed at $30\%$ ($\$1500$), giving $\$5788$ total tax.
common_misconceptions.counter_example: At $\$50\,000$ taxable income, the effective average tax rate is $\frac{5788}{50\,000} = 11.576\%$, far below $30\%$.

common_misconceptions.title: Dividing Annual Salary by 48 Instead of 52 to Find Weekly Pay
common_misconceptions.misconception: Assuming $1\text{ month} = 4\text{ weeks}$ and dividing an annual salary by $48$ (or multiplying weekly pay by $4$ to get monthly pay).
common_misconceptions.correct_concept: A standard year has $52$ weeks ($365 \div 7 \approx 52.14$), not $48$. Always convert between weekly and monthly via the annual figure.
common_misconceptions.counter_example: For a $\$62\,400$ annual salary, true weekly pay is $\$62\,400 \div 52 = \$1200$, whereas dividing by $48$ falsely gives $\$1300$.

fluency_and_understanding.question: Noah earns a normal wage of $\$25\text{/h}$. In one week he works $36$ normal hours and $6$ hours of overtime at time-and-a-half. Calculate his gross pay for the week.
Sienna earns a standard weekly wage of $\$1160$. She takes $4$ weeks of annual holiday leave and receives a $17.5\%$ leave loading on all $4$ weeks. Find her total holiday pay.
step_by_step_solution: Multiply by $1.175$ to include the $17.5\%$ leave loading: $4640 \times 1.175 = \$5452$ (loading is $\$812$).

fluency_and_understanding.question: A car salesperson is paid a monthly retainer of $\$1800$ plus $3.5\%$ commission on all vehicle sales. How much does he earn in a month where he sells cars worth $\$140\,000$?
Using the 2024–25 Australian tax bracket for $\$18\,201\text{–}\$45\,000$ ($16\text{c}$ for each $\$1$ over $\$18\,200$), calculate the income tax payable on a taxable income of $\$38\,200$.
step_by_step_solution: Find the excess taxable income over the $\$18\,200$ tax-free threshold: $38\,200 - 18\,200 = \$20\,000$.

problem_solving_and_modelling.question: A nurse in Hobart earns $\$40\text{/h}$ for a standard $38$-hour week. Overtime on Saturdays is paid at time-and-a-half, and overtime on Sundays is paid at double time. In one week she works $38$ normal hours, $5$ hours on Saturday, and $h$ hours on Sunday, earning a gross pay of $\$2140$. Find $h$.
step_by_step_solution: Sunday double-time rate is $2 \times 40 = \$80\text{/h}$. Set up the equation: $1520 + 300 + 80h = 2140$.

problem_solving_and_modelling.question: An agricultural equipment agent in Shepparton receives a monthly retainer of $\$2200$ plus $5\%$ commission on all sales above a monthly quota of $\$30\,000$. What total value of sales must she achieve in a month to earn a gross monthly income of $\$6450$?
step_by_step_solution: Subtract the retainer to find the required commission: $6450 - 2200 = \$4250$.

problem_solving_and_modelling.question: Marcus has a taxable income of $\$150\,000$. Using the 2024–25 bracket ($\$135\,001\text{–}\$190\,000$: $\$31\,288$ plus $37\text{c}$ for each $\$1$ over $\$135\,000$) and the $2\%$ Medicare levy, calculate his total tax + Medicare levy, and hence find his net annual after-tax income.
problem_solving_and_modelling.context: Net Income After Tax and Medicare

problem_solving_and_modelling.question: During the year, an employer withheld $\$410$ per week in PAYG tax instalments for $52$ weeks from a worker whose final taxable income was $\$85\,000$. Using the 2024–25 tax rule ($\$4288 + 30\%$ of excess over $\$45\,000$) plus the $2\%$ Medicare levy, determine whether the worker receives a tax refund or owes a tax bill, and state the exact dollar amount.
problem_solving_and_modelling.context: PAYG Tax Refund vs Balance Payable
step_by_step_solution: Total PAYG tax withheld over $52$ weeks $= 52 \times 410 = \$21\,320$.
Since $\$21\,320 > \$17\,988$, the worker receives a tax refund of $21\,320 - 17\,988 = \$3332$.

reasoning_and_communication.question: Verify mathematically where the base tax figure of $\$4288$ at the start of the $\$45\,001\text{–}\$135\,000$ bracket comes from in the 2024–25 Australian tax table.
step_by_step_solution: In the previous bracket ($\$18\,201\text{–}\$45\,000$), the width of the bracket is $45\,000 - 18\,200 = \$26\,800$.
Taxing that entire $\$26\,800$ slice at $16\text{c}$ per dollar gives $0.16 \times 26\,800 = \$4288$.

reasoning_and_communication.question: A worker whose taxable income is $\$75\,000$ (in the $30\%$ marginal tax bracket, plus $2\%$ Medicare levy) buys a $\$500$ textbook and professional tool kit that is an allowable work-related deduction. Explain why this deduction reduces their total tax + Medicare bill by $\$160$, not $\$500$.
reasoning_and_communication.final_answer: A deduction reduces taxable income by $\$500$, saving the combined marginal tax and Medicare rate of $32\%$ ($0.32 \times \$500 = \$160$)
step_by_step_solution: A tax deduction is subtracted from gross income before tax is calculated, reducing taxable income from $\$75\,000$ to $\$74\,500$.
Since each marginal dollar in this bracket is taxed at $30\%$ income tax plus $2\%$ Medicare levy ($32\%$ total), the tax saved is $0.32 \times 500 = \$160$.

reasoning_and_communication.question: Job Offer A pays a flat salary of $\$1250$ per week. Job Offer B pays a weekly retainer of $\$550$ plus $7\%$ commission on all weekly sales $S$. Write an equation to find the weekly sales $S$ at which both offers pay the same amount, and state when Offer B is better.
reasoning_and_communication.final_answer: $S = \$10\,000$; Offer B is better whenever weekly sales exceed $\$10\,000$
step_by_step_solution: Equate the two weekly pay expressions: $550 + 0.07S = 1250$.
Solve $0.07S = 700 \implies S = \$10\,000$. Whenever weekly sales exceed $\$10\,000$, Offer B pays more.

reasoning_and_communication.question: Define the effective (average) income tax rate as $\frac{\text{Income Tax Payable}}{\text{Taxable Income}} \times 100\%$ (excluding Medicare). Find the exact taxable income $T$ in the $\$45\,001\text{–}\$135\,000$ bracket at which a resident's effective income tax rate equals exactly $20\%$.
